title: Spectral cohort batcher - KV residency control for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Anika Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching on mixed prompt/response workloads creates transient KV cache pressure and GPU slab fragmentation. Short-turn requests are frequently coalesced with long-turns leading to eviction churn, KV miss spikes, and tail latency regressions. Goal: Implement a scheduling layer that forms short-lived request cohorts ("spectral cohorts") using lightweight histograms of sequence-length/response-length ratios and time-windowed affinity so we can pin/reserve KV residency per cohort and reduce eviction churn without harming throughput.
acceptance_criteria: 99th-percentile generation latency for small-turn (<64 tokens) requests improves by >= 12% compared to baseline continuous scheduler under mixed workload trace
KV eviction churn (evictions/min) reduced by >= 30% during 2x traffic bursts in replayed production trace
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab-free bytes / total) improves or remains within 5% of baseline during steady-state
No increase in average end-to-end cost per 1k tokens by more than 3% for the evaluated model family

notes: Core idea: summarize recent requests in short sliding windows into 8-bin length histograms (prompt tokens, expected response tokens bucketed). Use a lightweight spectral/clustering heuristic (power iteration on co-occurrence sketch) to form 2-6 cohorts per GPU shard per epoch.

KV residency policy: each cohort receives a soft reservation budget (in bytes) proportional to recent residency hit-rate and cohort throughput. Reservations are elastic and can be loaned between cohorts with a global reclamation watermark to avoid OOMs.
Admission control: enforce a min-batch-fill ratio (configurable) to prevent cohorts from producing many undersized microbatches. If ratio not met, request falls back to global merge queue.
Warmup/Probation: new cohorts go through a probation where we prefetch prefix KV pages for top-N frequent contexts to avoid cold-start evictions. Probation length is tunable (default 3 windows).

Trade-offs: cohorting reduces eviction churn but increases scheduler complexity and telemetry cardinality. Also risks starving rare long sessions if reservations are too aggressive; mitigations include dynamic share capping and SLA-driven preemption rules.

Implementation plan: scheduler-only changes in this ticket; avoid runtime kernel modifications. If successful, follow-up ticket will expose persistent cohort heuristics to Dedicated customers as config knobs.
